_readme: Endpoint Log Monitor shared rules file. Edit this file to add your own fixes.
fixes[].codes   - hex (0x87D00324), signed (-2016410844), unsigned (2278556452) or MSI/Win32 (1618).
fixes[].match   - case-insensitive regex used when no error code is found.
fixes[].title   - short issue title shown in the Issues table.
fixes[].logs    - log files this usually appears in (cosmetic).
noise           - regex patterns for lines that are harmless; always hidden.
hidden          - patterns you added with right-click > Hide for the whole team.

fixes.title: App installed but detection method did not find it
steps: Check the exit code and command line in AppEnforce.log. Confirm the installer actually ran to completion.
See which detection clause failed in AppDiscovery.log - the rule must be evaluated AFTER the install finishes.
Check 32-bit vs 64-bit paths and registry redirection (HKLM\Software vs HKLM\Software\Wow6432Node).
Confirm the exit code is listed in the deployment type Success codes - 3010 and 1641 are successes.
If the installer runs per-user but ConfigMgr runs it as SYSTEM, the detection hive/path will not match. Align the context.
Re-run the Application Deployment Evaluation Cycle from the Client Actions tab.

fixes.title: App still detected after uninstall completed
steps: Read AppEnforce.log and confirm the Uninstall command line actually ran and what it returned.
Run the uninstall string manually under the same context (SYSTEM vs user) the client used.
Look for leftover detection artifacts - files, registry values or the MSI product code - and remove them.
Check whether the uninstall requires a reboot before detection flips to false.
Re-run the Application Deployment Evaluation Cycle after cleanup.

fixes.title: Application deployment metadata was not found in WMI
steps: Confirm the ConfigMgr client WMI namespace responds: Get-CimInstance -Namespace root\ccm -ClassName SMS_Client.
Check for a half-removed client (ccmsetup.exe /uninstall left a partial install).
Run the Machine Policy Retrieval and Evaluation Cycle to republish deployment metadata.
If WMI is broken, repair the client from the Client Actions tab.

fixes.title: Application requirement or detection evaluation failed
steps: Open AppIntentEval.log and find the requirement rule that returned an error rather than False.
Test the requirement/detection query by hand (PowerShell Get-CimInstance or reg query) on a healthy device.
Confirm the WMI class or registry key exists on every OS build you target.
Fix the rule and redeploy, then force a machine policy refresh.

fixes.title: Unexpected error evaluating the detection rules
steps: Open the deployment type Detection Method and re-validate the rule expression XML.
Check AppDiscovery.log for the exact clause that failed to evaluate.
Simplify the rule to a single clause to isolate the bad one.
Redeploy and force a Machine Policy Retrieval and Evaluation Cycle.

fixes.title: Incorrect XML expression in the detection rules
steps: Open the Detection Method editor - the XML is malformed (unclosed element or bad nesting).
Rebuild the rule from scratch rather than hand-editing the XML.
Save, redeploy, then run the Application Deployment Evaluation Cycle.

fixes.title: Invalid operator in the detection rule
steps: Open the Detection Method and check the operator on each clause (Equals, Greater than, Exists ...).
Numeric operators cannot be used on string values - change the data type or the operator.
Redeploy and force a client policy refresh.

fixes.title: Unsupported data type in the detection rule
steps: Open the Detection Method and confirm the value type matches the registry value type (REG_DWORD vs REG_SZ).
A DWORD compared as a string always fails - correct the type.
Redeploy and re-evaluate the application.

fixes.title: Detection rules use an unsupported WMI namespace
steps: The WMI namespace in the detection rule is not usable by the client (for example a vendor namespace that does not exist on x64).
Test the query on a healthy client: Get-CimInstance -Namespace <ns> -Query <wql>.
Switch the detection method to Registry or Script if the namespace cannot be supported.
Redeploy and force a Machine Policy Retrieval and Evaluation Cycle.

fixes.title: Intune Win32 app detection rules not present
steps: The Win32 app package has no detection rule, or the rule was stripped during repackaging.
Open the app in Intune admin center > Apps > Windows and confirm a Detection rule is configured.
Re-upload the .intunewin package with a valid detection rule.
Force a sync from Settings > Accounts > Access work or school > Info > Sync.

fixes.title: Intune Win32 app enforcement error (detection/state)
steps: Read AppWorkload.log for the Applicability / Status / ErrorCode triple for the app.
Verify the detection rule manually under the same user context the install runs in.
Confirm the installer exit code is in the app's Success codes list.
Add AV exclusions for %windir%\IMECache and C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Intune Management Extension\Content.
Force a device sync and re-check AppWorkload.log.

fixes.title: Win32 app exit code is not mapped in the success list
steps: Open the app in Intune > Properties > Requirements and add the installer's exit code to Success codes.
3010 and 1641 mean success with a reboot - they must be listed or a good install is reported as failed.
Read the installer's own log to find the real exit code, then re-run the app.
Force a sync and check AppWorkload.log for the new ErrorCode.

fixes.title: Installer returned an exit code that is not mapped on the Win32 app
steps: Read the actual exit code from AppWorkload.log or IntuneManagementExtension.log.
Add that exit code to the app's Success codes in Intune if the installer really succeeded.
If it is a real failure, open the vendor installer log (MSI verbose log) and search for 'value 3' to find the failing action.
Repackage and reassign the app, then force a device sync.

fixes.title: Script execution timed out
steps: Read AppEnforce.log for the actual elapsed run time of the script or installer.
Raise the Maximum allowed run time (minutes) on the deployment type / Intune app.
Make sure the maintenance window or service window is longer than that run time.
For Intune remediations, shorten the script or split it - the IME hard timeout is short.

fixes.title: Failed to verify the executable or build the command line
steps: Check the Installation command line for broken quoting - an unbalanced quote produces exactly this error.
Confirm the content actually downloaded: look at CAS.log and ContentTransferManager.log.
Verify the setup file exists in ccmcache and is not blocked/quarantined by antivirus.
Redistribute the content and re-run the deployment.

fixes.title: Failed to access all the provided program locations (retryable)
steps: Review LocationServices.log for the 'Distribution Point=' entries - the client found DPs but cannot reach them.
Check boundary groups: the client must be in a group with a reachable DP.
Test from the client: browse http://<DP>/SMS_DP_<SiteCode>$/ and the SMB content path.
This code is retryable - only the final state after retries matters.
If it never resolves, refresh content locations and check the DP's IIS/SMB permissions.

fixes.title: Content not found
steps: Confirm the content exists on a DP: Software Library > Deployment Packages > Content Status. Redistribute if missing.
Check LocationServices.log for the DP list the client resolved - wrong boundary group, VPN or firewall is the usual cause.
Check DataTransferService.log for the transfer error (404 vs auth vs timeout) - each needs a different fix.
Verify the DP IIS/SMB share permissions and that the package ID matches.
Refresh content locations, then retry the deployment.

fixes.title: No service window exists to install software updates
steps: Open UpdatesDeployment.log and find the assignment - confirm the maintenance window on the collection.
Check the client time zone against the window; an offset window silently never opens.
Extend the window, or enable immediate installation / 'execute schedules outside service windows' for required updates.
If no window is configured at all, set one on the target collection.
Re-evaluate the deployment once the window opens.

fixes.title: Group Policy conflicts with Configuration Manager / WSUS
steps: Run gpresult /h report.html and look under Windows Components > Windows Update - a GPO is setting WUServer/WUStatusServer.
ConfigMgr client settings and GPO Windows Update settings fight each other; pick one owner for the workload.
Check HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate and ...\AU for UseWUServer and NoAutoUpdate.
If the device is co-managed, confirm the Windows Update Policies workload is assigned to ConfigMgr or Intune, not both.
Re-run the Software Updates Scan Cycle from the Client Actions tab after correcting policy.

fixes.title: Software updates installation not allowed at this time
steps: A service window, deadline or power setting is blocking installation.
Check the collection's maintenance window and the deployment deadline in UpdatesDeployment.log.
Confirm the device is not on battery / asleep if a restart is required.
Adjust the window or deadline and re-evaluate.

fixes.title: Software update scan tool not found in the job queue
steps: The scan job was cancelled or superseded before it completed - usually a restart or a second scan overlapping.
Trigger the Software Updates Scan Cycle again from the Client Actions tab.
If it repeats, restart the CCM client service and re-run the scan.
Check WindowsUpdate.log for the underlying WU agent failure.

fixes.title: Failed to trigger the installation of software updates
steps: Confirm there is an active deployment with a deadline for this device.
Check for a service window or a pending restart blocking the install.
Verify the Windows Update Agent is healthy (wuauserv running) and re-run the scan.
Trigger the Software Updates Agent Assignment Evaluation Cycle.

fixes.title: Windows Update returned HTTP 503 - service unavailable
steps: WUAHandler only reports what Windows Update returns - open WindowsUpdate.log for the real HTTP call.
Check the WSUS/SUP IIS 'WsusPool' application pool; a recycled or crashed pool produces 503.
Increase the WsusPool recycle limits and IIS uploadReadAheadSize / queue length.
Check free disk space on the WSUS content drive - a full drive is the classic 503 cause.
Re-run the Software Updates Scan Cycle after the SUP is healthy.

fixes.title: Windows Update could not resolve the server name (DNS)
steps: Resolve the WSUS/SUP FQDN from the client: Resolve-DnsName <sup-host>.
Verify the SUP port (8530/8531) and that the GPO WUServer / WUStatusServer values match the real URL.
Check the client's DNS suffix search order and proxy exceptions.
Re-run the scan once name resolution works.

fixes.title: Windows Update returned HTTP 408 - request timeout
steps: The SUP/IIS could not answer in time - check the WsusPool application pool and IIS request queue.
Check WSUS content folder free space and IIS logging volume.
Look for a proxy or firewall in the path timing out the request.
Re-run the scan after tuning IIS.

fixes.title: Windows Update returned HTTP 401 - access denied
steps: Authentication to the SUP failed - check the IIS binding and whether the WSUS pool identity is correct.
If using a proxy, check the credentials configured for it.
Verify the client certificate if the site is HTTPS.
Re-run the scan.

fixes.title: Windows Update returned HTTP 403 - forbidden
steps: The SUP refused the request - check IIS IP/domain restrictions and the WSUS self-update folder permissions.
Confirm the SUP is still a valid Software Update Point on the site.
Check that the WSUS content directory ACLs were not changed.
Re-run the scan.

fixes.title: Windows Update returned HTTP 407 - proxy authentication required
steps: Set the machine WinHTTP proxy correctly: netsh winhttp set proxy proxy-server="direct" or the real proxy.
Add the WSUS/SUP host to the proxy bypass list.
Check the ConfigMgr client proxy settings under Client Settings > Network Access.
Re-run the scan.

fixes.title: Windows Update data store has no data (WU_E_DS_NODATA)
steps: Update metadata the agent asked for is not in its local database - usually corrupt or never-synchronised metadata.
Force a SUP synchronisation from the console and confirm the update classification is published.
Reset the data store: stop wuauserv, BITS and CryptSvc; delete C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution\DataStore and \Download; restart; re-scan.
Run DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /ScanHealth and sfc /scannow.
Confirm the Windows Installer service is running.

fixes.title: Windows Update agent stopped mid-operation (WU_E_SERVICE_STOP)
steps: Read WindowsUpdate.log around the timestamp to see what stopped the agent (shutdown, restart, another installer).
Check whether a pending reboot or an MSI stopped wuauserv during the scan.
Confirm no third-party tool is stopping the Windows Update service.
Re-run the scan; if it stops every time, look at connectivity and policy retry intervals.

fixes.title: Windows Update disabled by policy - unmanaged server (WU_E_WU_DISABLE)
steps: Run gpresult /h report.html - a GPO is disabling Windows Update or pointing at an unmanaged server.
Compare ConfigMgr client settings for Software Updates against GPO settings; they conflict.
Check HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate and ...\AU for UseWUServer / NoAutoUpdate.
If co-managed, make sure the Windows Update Policies workload belongs to exactly one authority.
Re-run the scan after correcting policy.

fixes.title: Network timeout contacting the update/content server (WinHTTP 12002)
steps: Check basic connectivity: can the client reach the MP/DP/WSUS host on the required port?
Look for proxy, VPN or firewall interference - WinHTTP timeouts are almost always in-path.
Check for MTU/VPN issues on roaming devices.
Increase timeouts only after connectivity is proven.

fixes.title: Secure connection to the server failed (WinHTTP 12007)
steps: Verify the server name resolves and the TLS handshake succeeds (test with Invoke-WebRequest from the client).
Confirm the client trusts the server certificate chain (root CA in Trusted Root).
Check system time/clock skew - it breaks TLS.
Confirm the certificate has not expired and the IIS binding is correct.

fixes.title: TLS/certificate trust failure getting DP or update locations
steps: Classic HTTPS trust failure: 'GetDPLocations failed with error 0x80072f8f' after a WinHTTP request fails.
Confirm the client trusts the DP/MP certificate - the issuing root CA must be in the client's Trusted Root store.
Compare CCMHTTPSTATE / CCMHTTPSSTATE echoed in ccmsetup.log against the actual site communication mode.
Check system time for clock skew and confirm the server certificate is not expired.

fixes.title: Fatal Windows Installer error (MSI 1603)
steps: Open the MSI log (client.msi.log or the app's own verbose log) and search for 'value 3' - that names the failing custom action.
ccmsetup.log 'InstallFromManifest failed 0x80070643' and AppEnforce.log 'ExitCode: 1603' are the same failure in two encodings.
Common root causes: pending reboot, another install in progress (MSI 1618), insufficient rights, corrupt WMI.
Check msiexec.exe is not already running.
Capture a verbose MSI log by re-running the installer manually with /l*v install.log.

fixes.title: The system cannot find the file specified (Win32 2)
steps: In ccmsetup.log this usually means MobileClientUnicode.tcf or the install source is missing - a partial/aborted install.
Check C:\Windows\ccmsetup\ for a stale or partial folder.
Verify the source package (/source: or the MP) is reachable and the content finished downloading.
Confirm antivirus/FSRm is not quarantining the file.
In AppEnforce.log, confirm the install command points at a file that exists in ccmcache.

fixes.title: Access denied (Win32 5)
steps: Confirm the client is running the install as SYSTEM (ConfigMgr default) and that the target path/registry hive is writable.
Check folder and registry ACLs on the install destination.
Look for antivirus or AppLocker/WDAC blocking the writer.
For content download, check the DP share and NTFS permissions.

fixes.title: WMI invalid namespace (WBEM_E_INVALID_NAMESPACE)
steps: Test the namespace: Get-CimInstance -Namespace root\ccm -ClassName SMS_Client. If this fails the client WMI is broken.
Check WMI repository integrity: winmgmt /verifyrepository.
Repair first, do not delete: winmgmt /resyncrepository, then re-register the CCM provider.
If unrecoverable: ccmsetup.exe /uninstall, remove C:\Windows\CCM, repair WMI, reinstall the client.

fixes.title: WMI invalid class (WBEM_E_INVALID_CLASS)
steps: The class is not registered - typical of a half-installed or partially removed client.
Verify with: Get-CimClass -Namespace root\ccm -ClassName SMS_Client.
Run winmgmt /verifyrepository and winmgmt /resyncrepository.
Reinstall the client: ccmsetup.exe /uninstall then a clean install.

fixes.title: WMI access denied (WBEM_E_ACCESS_DENIED)
steps: Confirm the account running the query has local administrator rights.
Check DCOM launch/access permissions if you are querying the device remotely.
Verify the WMI repository ACLs were not modified by a hardening policy.
Retry locally to isolate whether it is a remote-only permission problem.

fixes.title: WMI object not found (WBEM_E_NOT_FOUND)
steps: Usually a missing client object or a certificate request that has not been created yet.
In ClientIDManagerStartup.log check the 'RegTask:' lines for the step that failed.
Force registration: run ccmsetup.exe /register, restart CcmExec, then run Machine Policy Retrieval and Evaluation.
If it persists, check client certificate state in certlm.msc.

fixes.title: WMI out of memory (WBEM_E_OUT_OF_MEMORY)
steps: Check available memory and the number of concurrent WMI queries.
Restart the Windows Management Instrumentation service (Winmgmt).
Look for a WMI provider leak from a third-party agent.
Repair the repository if the condition persists.

fixes.title: Unspecified failure (E_FAIL)
steps: E_FAIL is a placeholder, never a diagnosis - read the line immediately before it for the component-specific error.
In LocationServices.log check whether the client resolved an MP at all.
In ccmsetup.log find the preceding 'CcmSetup failed with error code' line.
Fix the underlying cause, then trigger the relevant client cycle again.

fixes.title: Unexpected error (E_UNEXPECTED)
steps: E_UNEXPECTED is a catch-all - always read the surrounding lines for the real component error.
Check whether the expected policy documents exist (0x87D00440 is the specific code for missing policy).
Trigger a Machine Policy Retrieval and Evaluation Cycle after fixing the cause.
If policy download is failing, verify MP connectivity and the client certificates.

fixes.title: Expected policy documents are incomplete or missing
steps: The client could not download a complete policy assignment set from the MP.
Check PolicyAgent.log for the download error and confirm the MP is reachable.
Trigger Machine Policy Assignments Request, then Machine Policy Evaluation.
Check for a site signing certificate problem or an MP returning HTTP errors.

fixes.title: Deployment metadata not available on the client
steps: The deployment was referenced by policy but its metadata never arrived.
Trigger Machine Policy Retrieval and Evaluation to republish assignments.
Confirm the deployment is still targeted at this collection and not expired.
Check PolicyAgent.log for download failures.

fixes.title: Not enough disk space to download content (cache/disk full)
steps: Check free space on the drive holding ccmcache.
Increase the client cache size: Client Settings > Cache Settings, or clear old content from ccmcache.
ContentTransferManager.log shows requested vs available size.
Trim the content package if it contains unnecessary files.
Retry the deployment.

fixes.title: Client cache is smaller than the requested content
steps: Raise the cache size in Client Settings > Cache Settings (default is only 100 MB).
Or run Clear Content on the deployment and free space in ccmcache.
Confirm the content package is not bloated.
Retry after the cache is large enough.

fixes.title: Content transfer manager job is in an unexpected state
steps: Find the job ID in ContentTransferManager.log and note the state transition that failed.
Restart the BITS service - CTM is BITS-backed.
Clear ccmcache (or use Clear Content on the deployment) and retry.
Check LocationServices.log for a stale or unreachable DP.
As a last resort reset the BITS/CTM job store and force a policy + deployment re-evaluation.

fixes.title: No WDS session is available for multicast
steps: Multicast requires the Windows Deployment Services role on the DP.
Confirm WDS is installed, started and at the same version as ConfigMgr; restart the WDSServer service.
If you do not use multicast, disable it on the package - most teams do not need it.
Redistribute the content after changing multicast settings.

fixes.title: Multicast (MCS) encountered a WDS error
steps: Check the WDS server role and the WDSServer service state on the DP.
Verify the DP and WDS versions match the site version.
Review the WDS remote installation log on the DP.
Disable multicast on the package if the feature is unused.

fixes.title: Intune app install has failed
steps: Read AppWorkload.log for the Applicability / Status / ErrorCode triple.
Open the installer's own log - for MSI, search for 'value 3'.
Confirm the exit code is in the app's Success codes.
Add AV exclusions for %windir%\IMECache and the Intune Management Extension content folder.
Force a device sync and re-check.

fixes.title: User installed the app before the managed install could take place
steps: Uninstall the manually installed copy from the device.
On the next sync Intune will install the managed version.
Use a detection rule and requirement that detect the unmanaged copy so remediation is automatic.

fixes.title: User rejected the offer to install the app
steps: This is a user decision on an Available assignment - no fix needed.
If the app must be present, change the assignment to Required.
For Required apps, re-evaluate: the IME will retry automatically.

fixes.title: User rejected the offer to update the app
steps: Expected behaviour for an Available update assignment.
Switch to a Required assignment if the update must be enforced.
Re-sync to re-offer.

fixes.title: Managed app was removed by the user
steps: For Available apps this is expected - nothing to fix.
For Required apps the IME will re-install; confirm the assignment is Required.
Check ClientHealth.log if re-installation never happens.

fixes.title: Intune app state is unknown
steps: Force a sync from Settings > Accounts > Access work or school > Info > Sync.
Check IME service health in ClientHealth.log.
Re-run the detection rule manually under the correct user context.
Restart the Intune Management Extension service.

fixes.title: Connection to Intune timed out
steps: Verify the device can reach the Intune service endpoints and is not blocked by a proxy.
Check for TLS inspection breaking the connection.
Confirm the device has working internet connectivity.
Force a sync and retry.

fixes.title: App is installed on the device but is unmanaged
steps: Uninstall the pre-existing copy from the device.
On the next sync the device installs the app from Intune.
Add a detection rule that identifies the unmanaged version so this is handled automatically.

fixes.title: Remote content was not found at the server (404)
steps: The content link expired or the package was deleted/re-uploaded.
Re-upload the .intunewin package or re-create the app.
Force a device sync so the IME gets a fresh content URI.
Check that the delivery optimization / BITS cache is not serving a stale entry.

fixes.title: Remote server required authentication and refused the credentials
steps: Confirm the device is signed in with a work/school account and has a valid token.
Check whether a proxy is intercepting the request.
Sign out and back in to the work account, then re-sync.

fixes.title: Access to remote content denied
steps: Check the app's assignment and that the device/user is in the target group.
Verify conditional access or an app protection policy is not blocking the download.
Re-sync and retry.

fixes.title: Connection to the remote server timed out
steps: Check internet connectivity and proxy/VPN configuration on the device.
Test reachability of the Intune content endpoints from the device.
Retry the sync after connectivity is confirmed.

fixes.title: Remote server refused the connection
steps: A network device or proxy is resetting the connection.
Check firewall rules and TLS inspection exclusions for Intune endpoints.
Confirm the device's system clock is correct.

fixes.title: Not enough disk space for the content
steps: Free disk space on the system drive.
Clear %windir%\IMECache and stale content in the Intune Management Extension content folder.
Retry the app installation.

fixes.title: Intune returned 404 - object not found
steps: The app, policy or assignment referenced no longer exists in the tenant.
Confirm the app still exists and is assigned.
Re-sync the device to pick up the current object set.

fixes.title: Remediation failed (for example BitLocker recovery password rotation)
steps: Open HealthScripts.log to see which remediation script failed and its output.
Confirm the script runs under the expected context and has the rights it needs.
For BitLocker: check TPM availability (Get-TPM), that WinRE is enabled (reagentc /info), and Secure Boot.
Check for a GPO that conflicts with the Intune BitLocker policy.
Force a device sync after fixing.

fixes.title: Remediation not applicable for this device
steps: The detection script returned 0, so no remediation ran - this is normally correct.
If you expected it to run, check the detection script logic and the scope tags/assignment group.

fixes.title: Sideloading is not enabled on this system
steps: Enable app sideloading: Settings > Privacy & security > For developers, or via policy.
Group Policy: Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > App Package Deployment > Allow all trusted apps to install.
Re-run the installation after the policy applies.

fixes.title: MDM sync failed with Invalid Request (HTTP 400)
steps: Often stale enrollment state, for example a device previously enrolled as Hybrid Azure AD joined that was re-enrolled.
Scheduled Tasks > Microsoft > Windows > EnterpriseMgmt - find the enrollment ID folder and delete stale entries, then re-enroll.
Verify the UPN under the enrollment registry key and that the device object exists in Entra ID.
Check the MDM device certificate expiry in certlm.msc.
Force a sync after cleanup.

fixes.title: Intune enrollment/sync error (not officially documented)
steps: Microsoft does not publish a definition for this code; community reports associate it with auto-enrollment failures.
Check that the device is licensed for Intune and that the MDM enrollment scope includes it.
Confirm the user's UPN and that auto-enrollment GPO/Intune settings are correct.
Review the DeviceManagement-Enterprise-Diagnostics-Provider event log for the surrounding entries.

fixes.title: Another installation is already in progress (MSI 1618)
steps: msiexec is single-instance per machine - a concurrent install is blocking this one.
Check whether msiexec.exe is running and what it is installing.
Sequence the apps or add a retry with backoff in the deployment.
Re-run the Application Deployment Evaluation Cycle once the other install finishes.

fixes.title: Windows Installer service could not be accessed (MSI 1601)
steps: Confirm the Windows Installer service (msiserver) is set to Manual and running.
Check whether a policy disables the installer service.
Restart msiserver and retry.

fixes.title: User cancelled the installation (MSI 1602)
steps: An interactive prompt appeared and was dismissed - make the install silent.
Repackage with fully silent switches (for example /qn or /quiet).
If it must be interactive, deploy as Available rather than Required.

fixes.title: Installation package could not be opened (MSI 1619)
steps: The MSI did not arrive intact - this is a content problem, not an install problem.
Check CAS.log and ContentTransferManager.log for the download result.
Confirm antivirus is not quarantining the file in ccmcache.
Redistribute the content and clear the local cache.

fixes.title: Installation package is not valid (MSI 1620)
steps: The file at the install path is not a valid MSI - wrong file, truncated download or renamed package.
Verify the file hash against the source.
Redistribute content and clear ccmcache before retrying.

fixes.title: Platform not supported by this MSI (MSI 1633)
steps: The package's Template Summary property does not support this architecture.
Check whether you are deploying an x86-only package to x64 devices.
Repackage with the correct platform or add a second deployment type with an architecture requirement.

fixes.title: Another version of this product is already installed (MSI 1638)
steps: The device has a different major version installed than the package you deployed.
Either allow upgrade by adding an upgrade code relationship, or uninstall the old version first.
Add 1638 to Success codes only if that really means success in your case.

fixes.title: Invalid command-line argument (MSI 1639)
steps: Check the Installation program string - a typo or bad switch produces this.
Test the exact command line manually from an elevated prompt.
Quote paths that contain spaces.

fixes.title: Success, reboot required (MSI 3010)
steps: This is a SUCCESS code - if it is not in Success codes, ConfigMgr/Intune reports a good install as failed.
Add 3010 to the deployment type / Intune app Success codes.
Schedule or allow a restart, then re-run detection - this is the classic cause of 0x87D00324 after a reboot-pending install.

fixes.title: Success, installer initiated a restart (MSI 1641)
steps: This is a SUCCESS code - add 1641 to Success codes.
Confirm the reboot is acceptable in the maintenance window.
Detection must run again after the restart.

fixes.title: Application deployment type handler could not be initialised
steps: The deployment type is not supported on this system (OS, architecture or installer type mismatch).
Check the deployment type's requirements and run this log on a device that matches your target.
Confirm the client is the current version - update the client if it is old.
Add a fallback deployment type for unsupported platforms.

fixes.title: Group Policy conflicts with Configuration Manager
steps: Run gpresult /h report.html and look under Windows Components > Windows Update.
ConfigMgr client settings and GPO Windows Update settings fight each other - pick one owner.
Check HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate for UseWUServer.
If co-managed, confirm the Windows Update Policies workload belongs to exactly one authority.
Re-run the Software Updates Scan Cycle after correcting policy.

fixes.match: (?i)exit\s*code[^.]{0,120}(isn't mapped|is not mapped|not mapped|not in the (list of )?success)
fixes.title: Installer returned an exit code that is not mapped on the Win32 app
steps: Read the actual exit code from the log.
Add it to the app's Success codes if the installer really succeeded (3010 and 1641 almost always should be there).
If it is a real failure, open the installer's own log and search for 'value 3' to find the failing action.
Repackage and reassign, then force a device sync.

fixes.match: (?i)app retry held by the .*GRS|24-hour GRS window|cooldown period
fixes.title: App retry held by the GRS (grace period) window
steps: The client will not retry an enforcement for up to 24 hours after a failure - this is by design.
If you need it sooner, trigger the Application Deployment Evaluation Cycle from the Client Actions tab.
For Intune, force a device sync to re-evaluate.
Fix the underlying install error first or it will simply fail again.

fixes.title: Client cannot locate a management point (name resolution)
steps: The client is falling back through AD > DNS > WINS > SLP and failing name resolution at each step.
Test resolution from the device: Resolve-DnsName <MP-FQDN>.
Confirm boundary groups so the client has a valid MP and DP.
Check ClientLocation.log first to see which site the client is assigned to.
Fix DNS/WINS, then trigger Location Services refresh.

fixes.match: (?i)scan failed with error|failed to end search job
fixes.title: Software update scan failed
steps: WUAHandler only reports what Windows Update returns - open WindowsUpdate.log for the real cause.
Decode the error on the Error codes tab (0x80244022 = HTTP 503, 0x8024402C = DNS, 0x8024401C = HTTP 408).
Check the SUP/WSUS health: IIS WsusPool application pool, disk space, self-update.
Re-run the Software Updates Scan Cycle from the Client Actions tab.

fixes.title: Client installation (ccmsetup) failed
steps: The last line of ccmsetup.log names the error code - decode it on the Error codes tab.
Check the Fallback Status Point STATEID echoed in the log to see which phase failed.
0x8007xxxx codes are Win32 errors - subtract 0x80070000 and run net helpmsg <n>.
Check the MP responds: http://<mp>/sms_mp/.sms_aut
For a clean retry: ccmsetup.exe /uninstall, delete C:\Windows\ccmsetup, then reinstall.

fixes.title: Client registration with the site failed
steps: The 'RegTask:' lines state exactly which registration step failed.
Registration cannot complete if the client cannot find an MP - fix boundary groups and DNS first.
Check for clock skew causing expired messages, and that CcmExec is running.
Check the client certificate in certlm.msc if the site is HTTPS.
Force it: ccmsetup.exe /register, restart CcmExec, then Machine Policy Retrieval and Evaluation.

fixes.title: Application enforcement failed
steps: Read the full AppEnforce.log entry - the parenthesised code names the specific failure.
Decode the code on the Error codes tab and follow its fix.
Confirm the install command line, exit code and detection method all agree.
Re-run the Application Deployment Evaluation Cycle from the Client Actions tab.

fixes.title: Policy download or refresh failed
steps: Check PolicyAgent.log for the HTTP status from the MP.
Verify the MP role is healthy and the client can reach it on the right port.
Check client certificates if the site uses HTTPS.
Trigger Machine Policy Assignments Request from the Client Actions tab.
